author: Rahul kp
title: Labour Variances
hook: who paid more, who took longer?
simple_words: Labour variance compares what labour should have cost with what it actually cost, and finds if rate or hours caused the gap.

definitions.meaning: Standard labour cost for actual output minus actual labour cost. It is the total of rate and efficiency effects (including idle time).
Standard rate multiplied by idle hours paid but not worked. It is always adverse.

key_points: ==Labour Rate Variance== arises from paying a different rate per hour than standard.
==Labour Efficiency Variance== arises from actual hours worked differing from standard hours for actual output.
!!Efficiency uses hours WORKED (excluding idle time)!!, while rate uses hours PAID.
Cost variance = Rate + Efficiency + Idle time (when idle time exists).
formula_hook: SR, AR, SH, AH - four letters!

formulas.name: Labour Cost Variance
formulas.legend: SH = standard hours for actual output; SR = standard rate/hr; AH paid = actual hours paid; AR = actual rate/hr. Positive = Favourable.

formulas.name: Labour Rate Variance
formulas.legend: Positive = Favourable, negative = Adverse. Uses hours paid.

formulas.name: Labour Efficiency Variance
formulas.legend: AH worked = AH paid − idle hours. Idle Time Variance = idle hours × SR (Adverse).

insight.text: LCV = LRV + LEV + Idle Time Variance, so check your answer by adding the parts.

memory_trick.explanation: Always write Standard first, Actual second. A positive answer is Favourable, a negative answer is Adverse. Do this for rate, efficiency and cost.

steps: Note AH paid, idle hours, AH worked
Idle time = idle hrs × SR; add to check
exam_tip: If idle time is given, use hours worked in efficiency and hours paid in rate. Check that LCV equals the sum of parts.

doubt.question: Why is idle time variance always adverse?
doubt.answer: Idle hours are paid but produce nothing, so cost is incurred with no output. It is shown as a loss, never as a gain.

mistakes.wrong: Using hours worked in the rate variance when idle time exists
mistakes.right: Rate variance uses actual hours paid: (SR − AR) × AH paid.

mistakes.wrong: Using budgeted output to find standard hours
mistakes.right: Standard hours are for actual output produced.

mistakes.wrong: Showing idle time variance as favourable
mistakes.right: Idle time variance is always adverse.

Checker 1: Insight text, Step 5 and Formula 3 legend: the idle time variance is written as 'idle hours × SR (Adverse)', which is a positive amount, but students are then told to add the parts to check LCV. For the check to work, the idle time variance must be entered as a negative (adverse) figure. Suggested wording: 'LCV = LRV + LEV + ITV, where ITV = −(idle hours × SR), so it is always adverse; add the parts using their signs.'

Checker 1: Definition 2 / doubt answer (wording only): it would help to say that this refers to abnormal idle time paid but not worked. Normal idle time is usually built into the standard hours. Suggested wording: 'Idle Time Variance = SR × abnormal idle hours paid but not worked; always adverse.'
